package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all Volusion-hosted stores with injected code)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to steal payment card details from end customers by intercepting sensitive data entered on checkout/payment forms and exfiltrating it to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This is a Magecart-style web skimmer attack, targeting thousands of online stores and their customers, resulting in large-scale payment card theft.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a customer loads and interacts with the checkout or payment page (specifically on form submission).
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the HTML or JavaScript of Volusion-hosted e-commerce sites, typically within a <script> tag or as an external JavaScript file loaded on payment pages.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user submits the checkout/payment form, the code attaches an event listener to the form, collects credit card data from specific input fields, encodes the data, and exfiltrates it via an HTTP request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in theft of payment card details.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive payment data directly from the browser and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled domain unrelated to payment processing. This behavior is a hallmark of Magecart web skimming attacks and is not present in legitimate e-commerce scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should never collect and transmit payment data to third-party or untrusted domains. Payment data should only be sent directly to trusted payment processors via secure, vetted integrations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may access payment fields for client-side validation or formatting, but should never transmit raw payment data externally except to authorized payment gateways using secure APIs.
key_indicators: Event listener attached to payment or checkout form submission
Direct collection of credit card fields (number, expiry, CVV) from the DOM
Outbound network request to a hardcoded, untrusted, or newly registered domain
Use of encoding functions (e.g., btoa) to obfuscate exfiltrated data
Creation of image beacons or similar covert exfiltration techniques

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to Volusion's infrastructure and injects malicious JavaScript into customer storefronts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded by end customers visiting affected Volusion-hosted stores.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the context of the checkout/payment page, hooking into the form submission event to intercept user input.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment card data from unsuspecting customers at the point of transaction.

attack_chain.action: Collected payment card data is encoded and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure via a network request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment card details, enabling further fraud or resale on underground markets.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code attaching event listeners to payment or checkout form submission events
Client-side scripts collecting credit card or payment data fields (e.g., number, expiry, CVV) from the DOM
Outbound network requests from payment pages to domains not associated with the legitimate merchant or payment processor
Use of encoding or obfuscation functions (such as btoa or base64) prior to data exfiltration
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently modified <script> tags in e-commerce site HTML, especially on checkout/payment pages
External JavaScript files loaded from untrusted, newly registered, or previously unseen domains
Presence of inline scripts with suspicious network activity or obfuscated code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from checkout or payment pages to domains unrelated to the merchant or payment processor (e.g., 'malicious-domain.com')
Use of image beacons or encoded GET requests (e.g., via new Image().src) to exfiltrate sensitive data
Network traffic containing base64-encoded payloads originating from payment forms
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor e-commerce sites for unauthorized or unexpected changes to JavaScript, especially scripts loaded on payment or checkout pages. Implement and enforce strict Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict allowed script sources. Analyze network traffic from checkout pages for outbound requests to unknown or untrusted domains, and inspect for scripts that access payment fields and transmit data externally. Use file integrity monitoring to detect changes to HTML and JavaScript files, and employ threat intelligence to identify newly registered or suspicious domains.
